nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set and $D \subseteq V$. If the complement $V \setminus D$ has at least two elements, then $D$ together with one new vertex has fewer elements than $V$, that is, $|D| + 1 < |V|$.
nodes.title: Cardinality bound for contracting the complement

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$ and a vertex $v \in V$, the collapse map from $V$ to $D$ together with the contraction vertex sends $v$ to the contraction vertex if and only if $v \notin D$.
nodes.title: Preimage of the contraction vertex under the collapse map

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$, a vertex $v \in V$ and an element $a \in D$, the collapse map from $V$ to $D$ together with the contraction vertex sends $v$ to $a$ if and only if $v = a$.
nodes.title: Preimages of retained vertices under the collapse map

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$, the collapse map from $V$ to $D$ together with the contraction vertex sends each $v \in D$ to $v$ itself.
nodes.title: The collapse map fixes the retained set

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$, the collapse map from $V$ to $D$ together with the contraction vertex sends each vertex $v \notin D$ to the contraction vertex.
nodes.title: The collapse map sends the complement to the contraction vertex

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$ whose complement $V \setminus D$ is nonempty, the collapse map from $V$ to $D$ together with the contraction vertex is surjective.
nodes.title: The collapse map is surjective

nodes.summary: For a set $D \subseteq V$, the collapse map sends $V$ to $D$ together with one new vertex, the contraction vertex: each $v \in D$ is sent to itself, and each $v \notin D$ is sent to the contraction vertex.
nodes.title: Collapsing the complement of a set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a 2-vertex-connected graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $D \subseteq V$ be a set with at least two elements that induces a connected subgraph of $G$ and whose complement $V \setminus D$ is nonempty. Then the graph obtained from $G$ by contracting $V \setminus D$ to a single vertex is 2-vertex-connected.
nodes.title: Contracting the complement preserves 2-connectivity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $V$, let $D \subseteq V$, and contract $V \setminus D$ to a single vertex. A vertex $a \in D$ is adjacent to the contraction vertex in the contracted graph if and only if $a$ is adjacent in $G$ to some vertex $v \notin D$.
nodes.title: Neighbors of the contraction vertex

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $V$, let $D \subseteq V$, and contract $V \setminus D$ to a single vertex. Two vertices $a, b \in D$ are adjacent in the contracted graph if and only if they are adjacent in $G$.
nodes.title: Contraction preserves adjacency among retained vertices

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ and let $D \subseteq V$. Contracting the complement of $D$ to a single vertex gives the simple graph whose vertices are the elements of $D$ together with one new vertex $\ast$, in which two vertices $a, b \in D$ are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in $G$, and a vertex $a \in D$ is adjacent to $\ast$ exactly when $a$ has a neighbour in $G$ outside $D$. nodes.title: Contracting the complement of a vertex set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is 2-vertex-connected, that is, $G$ has at least three vertices and stays connected after deleting at most one vertex. Let $H$ be the square of $G$: the graph on the same vertices in which two distinct vertices are adjacent if and only if they are adjacent in $G$ or have a common neighbour in $G$. nodes.title: Fleischner's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $x \in V$. Then $G$ has a strong square cycle at $x$ if the square $G^2$ of $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle that starts and ends at $x$ and whose two edges at $x$, its first and its last edge, are edges of $G$.
nodes.title: Strong square cycle at a vertex

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $x \in V$. Then $G$ has a strong square cycle at $x$ if and only if the square $G^2$ of $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle $p$ that starts and ends at $x$ such that $x$ is adjacent in $G$ to the second vertex of $p$ and the second-to-last vertex of $p$ is adjacent in $G$ to $x$.
nodes.title: Characterization of strong square cycles

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is 2-vertex-connected, that is, $G$ has at least three vertices and stays connected after deleting at most one vertex. nodes.title: Strengthened Fleischner theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
